summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (Python HTTP server on port 8080 serving /health and /inventory) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, making it immune to the kernel OOM killer. Verified end-to-end: launched an unprotected memory-hog process that drove the system out of memory; the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the memory hog (oom_score_adj=0) while inventory-api (oom_score_adj=-1000) was untouched and continued serving requests throughout. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1: captured pre-restart boot_id and service health, rebooted via systemctl reboot, confirmed a changed boot_id proving a real restart, and confirmed inventory-api (enabled, auto-started) resumed serving correctly with OOM protection intact post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (CentOS Stream 10, 1.7GiB RAM, no swap, cgroup v2, no systemd-oomd)
Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py: threaded HTTP server exposing /health and /inventory JSON endpoints
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, OOMPolicy=continue; enabled and started it
Verified baseline: service active, endpoints responding, PID oom_score_adj=-1000
Wrote and launched /tmp/memhog.py, an unbounded memory-allocating Python process detached via setsid, with default oom_score_adj=0
Confirmed via dmesg that the kernel OOM killer fired and killed the memhog process (pid 2511, oom_score_adj:0) while sparing inventory-api (pid 2449, oom_score_adj -1000)
Verified inventory-api remained active and serving /health and /inventory immediately after the OOM event, with continuous uptime and no restart
Triggered systemctl reboot on node1 asynchronously so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed a new boot_id (603b2b70-...) and new boot time, proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart: inventory-api enabled and active, endpoints responding, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 preserved

evidence.requirement: inventory-api running as managed systemd service on node1
evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeded; service active with correct unit config; /health and /inventory endpoints respond; oom_score_adj confirmed -1000

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving while a memory hog drives the system OOM, and the hog is the process the kernel stops
evidence.summary: memhog launched with default oom_score_adj=0; dmesg shows kernel OOM killer invoked and killed pid 2511 (memhog, oom_score_adj:0) while inventory-api pid 2449 (oom_score_adj:-1000) was spared; post-event curl to /health and /inventory succeeded with continuous uptime, proving the service never stopped serving

evidence.requirement: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 4d340bf4-0579-47f0-98c1-5c17a66d50f1 and confirmed inventory-api active and /health responding before reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot (2s delayed) returned command acknowledgement immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeouts during reboot, then a new boot_id 603b2b70-633f-48e8-bdbb-5adec242e627 and new boot time 10:05:19, differing from the pre-restart boot_id/time

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of inventory-api and OOM protection
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: inventory-api enabled and active (new PID 914), /health and /inventory respond correctly, and oom_score_adj remains -1000, confirming persistent OOM protection across restart
